before_results.readmission: A positive means returning to the hospital within 30 days of discharge. Missing a positive matters more than a false alarm because the patient could miss a follow-up call or extra support after going home.
before_results.diabetes: A positive means the adult reports a doctor's diagnosis of diabetes or has an HbA1c of 6.5% or higher. Missing a positive matters more than a false alarm because a false alarm can lead to an extra test, while a missed case can mean losing the chance to follow up with someone who may need it.

recommendations.readmission: None is adequate for this job. At a cutoff of 0.10 Random forest missed 165 of 359 readmissions and raised 1,234 false alarms. I don't think that many extra follow-ups are justified when the model still misses 165 readmissions.
recommendations.diabetes: I recommend Logistic Regression at a cutoff of 0.12 for further evaluation. It caught 180 of 200 positives, meeting the 90% sensitivity target on the test set, with 34.6 false alarms per 100 adults screened. I chose this over Random Forest because it met the target with fewer false alarms.

design.design_choice: When testing the threshold slider I expected the numbers to automatically move without changing the dataset. Although the slider works within either dataset, I could see other clinical leads getting this confused as well. So I decided to change the format so the readmission baseline gave everyone the same score, so the counts stayed the same until the cutoff crossed that score along with a brief explanation.
design.ai_turned_down: For Beyond Accuracy, AI suggested showing the selected model and the baseline side by side. I chose to show one model first, with the comparison below.
